description:
Found by fz-kdt.93 (2026-08-31, measured at 743319fb4 vs d5d45a074).

WHAT MOVED: on 00420_enum_take_drop_split, 13 recursive `direct_call ... -> return`
edges changed `return_flow=tail` into `return_flow=continue(shape{...})`, and
`fz.codegen.define_function` rose 1087 -> 1100. enum_predicate_search moves the
other way (5 continue -> tail, 2 tail -> continue; 658 -> 655 functions);
range_map does not move. No pinned budget moved (matrix 416/0, and none of the
three lens fixtures carries a budget assertion).

MECHANISM: at a cut position the layout comes from `cut_transport_layout`
(jobs/transport.rs). An ExecutableReturn with several origins usually still has
READABLE evidence beside the cut arm, and that evidence carries its type, so it
keeps the evidence form -- e.g. `lane({list(int), :false | :true})`. The
matching ReturnPayload for the same call has only the ONE cut origin, so it has
no evidence and falls back to the type contract, which decomposes an exact tuple
type -- `shape{lane(list), lane(:false | :true)}`. The artifact's
`CallReturnFlow` (jobs/artifact.rs, `ControlDestination::Return` arm) demands
source == caller_return == payload for a `Tail` and emits `Continue` otherwise,
so the caller re-materializes: it builds the pair unboxed at the callee and
boxes it again on the way out. Correct, but it is a per-call conversion on a hot
recursive edge.

Base did not have this because the knot group stamped ONE layout on every
member, which made the two agree by force -- the very lottery fz-kdt.93 removed.

DIRECTION: the two positions are two views of one calling convention and should
derive one contract. Either the payload should prefer its callee's published
return layout when that layout carries its type (a fact edge that is already in
the cone), or an ExecutableReturn inside a cut cycle should take the same type
contract its payload takes. Measure both against the three lens fixtures with
tools/canon-gate.sh: the target is 0 net tail -> continue with the 44 gained
decomposed forms kept.
title: A cut position's return and its caller's payload invent different contracts, so a recursive tail becomes a continue
